transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I... I came in because I can’t get this thought out of my head. I worked as an electrician for years, you know, I know what’s safe and what isn’t—or I thought I did. I used to be the guy people trusted with that stuff, wiring houses, checking panels, making sure nobody got hurt.

But if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then... I don’t know. It feels like maybe I’m dangerous to be around. Like anybody who works with me, or even lives under my roof, is taking a risk just being near me.
Can you tell me more about what happened with your brother, and how you feel about it now?

It was my brother, and… I keep going over it like there’s some loose wire I can find if I just think hard enough. That’s what I do, you know? You trace the circuit, you find the fault. I’ve done that a thousand times.

But now it’s just this… weight. Guilt, mostly. And anger too, like it sits right in my chest all day. I get mad at myself, mad at the whole situation, and then I feel worse for being mad.

And when I look at my nephew… God. I think about how he lost his dad, and somehow he got stuck with me instead. That’s the part I can’t shake.
Have you had times before when you felt this low or guilty, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

I mean… I’ve felt bad before, sure. Everybody does. Jobs go wrong, money gets tight, you get into it with family—my old foreman used to say if you don’t go home mad once in a while, you’re not working hard enough.

But this is different. It’s like there’s this heavy mix of guilt and anger sitting in my chest all day. Especially when I look at my nephew and think… he lost his dad, and he got stuck with me instead. I keep trying to tell myself that’s not a useful thought, like checking the same breaker over and over when you already know it’s tripped, but it doesn’t really let up.

You mentioned this feeling is different from normal frustration or sadness. Have you had episodes in the past where you felt this level of guilt or low mood, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I don’t… I don’t think I’ve ever had it like this before. I’ve felt guilty over things, sure—missed stuff on a job, snapped at somebody, all that normal life kind of thing. One time I wired a whole kitchen and the homeowner kept changing their mind about where they wanted the outlets, drove me half-crazy—but that’s just frustration, you know?

This now is different. It’s like this heavy mix of guilt and anger just sits in my chest all day. And it gets worse when I look at my nephew, because all I can think is… he lost his dad, and somehow he got stuck with me instead.
Have you ever had times in the past where your mood was low and stayed that way for weeks at a time, or this level of guilt that didn’t go away easily?

Not really like this, no. I’ve had rough stretches, sure—work slowing down, bills stacking up, some inspector making you redo something because he wants it a different way than the last guy did. That stuff can drag on you.

But this… this doesn’t clear out. It’s this heavy mix of guilt and anger sitting in my chest all day. I’ll be doing something normal, making coffee or checking a panel, and then I look at my nephew and it just hits me—he lost his dad, and he got stuck with me instead. And then I’m right back in it.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, like activities you used to like doing, either at work or at home?

I don’t know… I mean, I still do things. Work is work, you know? You don’t really “enjoy” crawling through an attic in July, but you do it because the wire’s not gonna pull itself.

At home, I guess I haven’t really been paying attention to what I like or don’t like. I’ll put something on TV and then realize I’m not following it, but that might just be because half the shows now are all over the place anyway. My nephew likes those superhero movies, and I’ll sit there with him, but I’m mostly just… sitting there.

So I don’t know if I’d call it not enjoying things. I just haven’t really thought about it that way.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like activities at work or hobbies at home?

I mean… I don’t really know. I hear what you’re asking, but I don’t sit around rating whether I’m enjoying things, you know?

Like at work, some parts were never exactly fun. Nobody’s taking up electrical work because they love fishing cable through insulation and getting dust down their shirt. And hobbies… I used to putter around the garage, fix little things, maybe start a project and leave half the screws in a coffee can somewhere. But lately it’s hard to tell if I don’t enjoy it or if I just don’t get around to it.

I guess I haven’t noticed it in a clean way, if that makes sense. Stuff just feels… not at the front of my mind.
Have you found that you don’t care about or look forward to things you used to enjoy, like specific tasks at work or projects you used to do for fun?

I’m not sure I could say that straight, like yes or no. I mean, I don’t wake up thinking, “Oh good, I get to do this job today,” but I don’t think most guys do, you know?

There are parts of work I used to feel good about, like when you clean up some mess of wiring somebody left behind and it finally looks right. But then again, half the time now I’m just trying to get through the list without somebody calling me about something else. And projects at home… I’ll look at something in the garage and think, “I should fix that,” and then I end up moving it from one bench to the other.

So… I don’t know if I don’t care, exactly. It’s more like I haven’t really been looking forward to much, but I couldn’t tell you if that’s the same thing you mean.
Looking back, would you say you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like certain tasks at work or projects you used to work on for fun?

I don’t know… looking back is tricky, because everything kind of blurs together. I’ll still go to work, still get things done if somebody’s paying me to do it. And sometimes a job comes out clean, and I can see that it’s clean, but I don’t know if that means I’m enjoying it or just noticing it’s done right.

At home, the projects are still sitting there. I’ve got this old shelf thing I meant to fix—well, it’s not even that old, my brother-in-law gave it to me because he was moving, and he never keeps anything, which drives my sister nuts—but anyway, it’s in the garage and I keep meaning to get to it.

So… lost interest? Maybe. I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I haven’t really been keeping track of what I enjoy.
Have you noticed that your mood has been low most of the day, nearly every day, since your brother passed?

Yeah… I mean, low is one way to say it, I guess. It’s not like I’m crying all day or something. It’s more like there’s this weight sitting right in my chest.

A lot of it is guilt, and anger too, which… I don’t even know who I’m mad at half the time. Then I’ll look at my nephew, and he’s just doing some normal kid thing, leaving his shoes in the middle of the room or asking what’s for dinner even though we just ate, and all I can think is—he lost his dad. And somehow he got me instead.

So yeah, most days it’s there. Maybe not “sad” exactly, but it’s heavy, and it doesn’t really leave me alone.
Have you had days where this heavy feeling in your chest and your mood being low lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks or more in a row?

Yeah… I mean, two weeks, sure. Honestly it’s hard to break it up like that, like on a calendar. I’m not sitting there marking days off, you know? I can barely remember if I paid the electric bill until I see the little email thing—funny, being an electrician and still almost missing that.

But yeah, that heavy feeling… it’s there most of the day. It’s like guilt and anger sitting right in my chest. Especially when I look at my nephew and I get stuck on this thought that he lost his dad, and somehow he got stuck with me instead. That doesn’t really just come and go for an afternoon. It hangs around.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have less energy than usual most of the time?

I don’t know. I mean, I’m tired a lot, but who isn’t, right? Work wears you down, and then you get home and there’s always something else that needs doing. The other day I sat down just to take my boots off and ended up staring at the wall for—I don’t even know how long.

But then again, that could just be because I’m getting older. My knees make noises now, which my uncle used to joke about, saying once your joints start talking back you’re officially done. He had this recliner that squeaked worse than he did.

So… less energy than usual? Maybe. I’m not sure what my usual even is anymore.
Have you found that you don’t really get any satisfaction or sense of accomplishment from things you used to feel good about, like finishing a job well or working on a project you used to enjoy?

I’m not sure. I mean… finishing a job still feels like finishing a job, you know? Like if the lights come back on or the panel’s labeled right, there’s that little moment of, okay, that’s done.

But satisfaction… I don’t know if I’d call it that. Sometimes I’m just thinking about the next thing I forgot to do. I used to like tinkering with stuff in the garage, fixing old radios and whatever, but half the time now I go out there and just move things from one bench to another. My brother used to tease me because I’d keep every little screw in coffee cans—said I was one step away from becoming our grandfather.

Sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I don’t know. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I feel proud of things lately.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I don’t really know. I mean, I eat when I remember to, mostly. Sometimes I’ll grab something from a gas station between jobs and then realize later that was basically dinner, but that’s not exactly new either.

Weight-wise… I haven’t been checking. My jeans still fit, I guess. Though work pants always shrink funny if you use the wrong dryer setting—my brother used to say that was my excuse every time after Thanksgiving.

So… I haven’t noticed anything major, no. Or if it’s changed, I don’t think I’ve been paying enough attention to say.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

Yeah… sleep’s been pretty bad, I guess. Most nights I’m just lying there, listening. Like for crackling sounds, or… if a car door shuts out in the driveway, I’m wide awake. Sometimes it’s nothing, just the house settling, but I can’t seem to stop checking it in my head.

And then when I do finally fall asleep, it doesn’t hold. I’ll jolt up soaked through, from dreams about the garage. Then I’m just sitting there, and it’s like, well, work starts in a few hours anyway.

I used to be able to sleep through anything. My dad said I slept through a tree limb coming down once when I was a kid, sounded like a cannon. Now a little noise and that’s it. I’m up. Going back to sleep doesn’t really happen much.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when your mood was low and stayed that way for at least two weeks in a row?

I don’t know… I’m trying to think back and it all kind of runs together. I’ve had rough stretches, sure. Everybody has, I guess. Like after jobs went bad or money got tight, I’d get down for a while.

But two weeks straight… I’m not sure I ever kept track of it like that. I’m not really the type to mark it on a calendar, you know? My mom used to write everything on those little wall calendars with the kittens on them—appointments, oil changes, birthdays—and I’d forget to even look at the thing.

So… before now, I can’t really say. Maybe, maybe not. I don’t have a clear memory of a solid two-week stretch like that.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for several weeks at a time?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had times where I wasn’t exactly cheerful, if that’s what you mean, but several weeks… I don’t know how I’d measure that.

I used to just keep working through stuff. You get up, go to the job, crawl around someone’s attic with insulation sticking to your arms, come home tired, and the days sort of blur. I remember one winter I barely did anything after work except sit around, but then again it was cold and dark by five, and everybody gets like that, right?

So… I can’t say for sure there was a period like that before. Nothing I can point to clearly.

It hangs around.

inference.note: This turn supports the presence of a major depressive episode with the duration and persistence of symptoms (e.g., heavy mood, guilt, loss of interest) over a period exceeding two weeks. The distinction between a first episode (F32.9) and a recurrent episode (F33.9) remains unclear based on the dialogue. No evidence to support continued consideration of F43.20 (Adjustment Disorder) given the depth and persistence of symptoms aligning more with a depressive disorder.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a decrease in energy or fatigue nearly every day, which would support a diagnosis of major depressive episode.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that you feel tired or have less energy than usual most of the time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about fatigue or low energy, which is not specifically covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know. I mean, I’m tired a lot, but who isn’t, right? Work wears you down, and then you get home and there’s always something else that needs doing. The other day I sat down just to take my boots off and ended up staring at the wall for—I don’t even know how long.

But then again, that could just be because I’m getting older. My knees make noises now, which my uncle used to joke about, saying once your joints start talking back you’re officially done. He had this recliner that squeaked worse than he did.

So… less energy than usual? Maybe. I’m not sure what my usual even is anymore.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities they used to enjoy, which would help distinguish between F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode) and F33.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent).
doctor.question: Have you found that you don’t really get any satisfaction or sense of accomplishment from things you used to feel good about, like finishing a job well or working on a project you used to enjoy?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about loss of satisfaction or pleasure in previously rewarding activities, which is not covered by the provided PTSD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean… finishing a job still feels like finishing a job, you know? Like if the lights come back on or the panel’s labeled right, there’s that little moment of, okay, that’s done.

But satisfaction… I don’t know if I’d call it that. Sometimes I’m just thinking about the next thing I forgot to do. I used to like tinkering with stuff in the garage, fixing old radios and whatever, but half the time now I go out there and just move things from one bench to another. My brother used to tease me because I’d keep every little screw in coffee cans—said I was one step away from becoming our grandfather.

Sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I don’t know. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I feel proud of things lately.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had a significant change in appetite or weight related to their mood
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about appetite or weight changes, which are not covered by any item in the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know. I mean, I eat when I remember to, mostly. Sometimes I’ll grab something from a gas station between jobs and then realize later that was basically dinner, but that’s not exactly new either.

Weight-wise… I haven’t been checking. My jeans still fit, I guess. Though work pants always shrink funny if you use the wrong dryer setting—my brother used to say that was my excuse every time after Thanksgiving.

So… I haven’t noticed anything major, no. Or if it’s changed, I don’t think I’ve been paying enough attention to say.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant change in sleep patterns, which is a key symptom in differentiating between major depressive disorder and other conditions.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I lie there listening for crackling or a car door in the driveway, and when I do fall asleep I jolt awake soaked through from dreams about the garage and can't get back down before work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about changes in sleep, including trouble falling asleep, waking during the night, and early awakening.

patient.answer:
Yeah… sleep’s been pretty bad, I guess. Most nights I’m just lying there, listening. Like for crackling sounds, or… if a car door shuts out in the driveway, I’m wide awake. Sometimes it’s nothing, just the house settling, but I can’t seem to stop checking it in my head.

And then when I do finally fall asleep, it doesn’t hold. I’ll jolt up soaked through, from dreams about the garage. Then I’m just sitting there, and it’s like, well, work starts in a few hours anyway.

I used to be able to sleep through anything. My dad said I slept through a tree limb coming down once when I was a kid, sounded like a cannon. Now a little noise and that’s it. I’m up. Going back to sleep doesn’t really happen much.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had a prior episode of depression lasting at least 2 weeks, which would support a diagnosis of F33.9 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder) over F32.9 (Single Episode Depression).
doctor.question: Before this current period, have you ever had a time when your mood was low and stayed that way for at least two weeks in a row?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about past episodes of sustained low mood for at least two weeks, which is not covered by the provided PTSD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I’m trying to think back and it all kind of runs together. I’ve had rough stretches, sure. Everybody has, I guess. Like after jobs went bad or money got tight, I’d get down for a while.

But two weeks straight… I’m not sure I ever kept track of it like that. I’m not really the type to mark it on a calendar, you know? My mom used to write everything on those little wall calendars with the kittens on them—appointments, oil changes, birthdays—and I’d forget to even look at the thing.

So… before now, I can’t really say. Maybe, maybe not. I don’t have a clear memory of a solid two-week stretch like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced previous episodes of major depression, which would support a diagnosis of F33.9 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for several weeks at a time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about past episodes of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting several weeks, which is not covered by the provided PTSD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had times where I wasn’t exactly cheerful, if that’s what you mean, but several weeks… I don’t know how I’d measure that.

I used to just keep working through stuff. You get up, go to the job, crawl around someone’s attic with insulation sticking to your arms, come home tired, and the days sort of blur. I remember one winter I barely did anything after work except sit around, but then again it was cold and dark by five, and everybody gets like that, right?

So… I can’t say for sure there was a period like that before. Nothing I can point to clearly.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-episode moderate depressive syndrome characterized by persistent guilt, anger, low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, sleep disturbance, and a heavy feeling in the chest most days for over two weeks. There is no clear history of prior depressive episodes, which argues against a recurrent course (F33.9). Symptoms appear to be a direct response to the traumatic loss of his brother and the associated guilt, but the absence of a formal PTSD stressor criterion (e.g., life-threatening event, actual or threatened death) and predominance of depressive features support major depressive disorder over adjustment or trauma-related disorders.
